action: Built wai-brief command: full synopsis mode + topic-focused mode. Topic mode gathers evidence from lugs/track/state, extracts options from existing record only, outputs paste-able brief. Registered in WAI-Skills.jsonl. Synced to .claude/commands/.
thinking: The phone-a-friend pattern is the outbound counterpart to chat-to-track (inbound). Key design constraint: options must come only from what exists in the record — not invented from general knowledge. This makes the brief trustworthy and traceable. The 'What I Need From You' field is deliberately left blank — user fills it in to shape the external conversation. Topic mode does keyword search across lugs + track + state to gather evidence, then structures it as: background (what we know), current state (where things stand), options (paths in the record), open questions (unresolved threads). This is a lightweight version of the consultation exchange eject packet — same concept, no network, no API, just a paste-able text block.
decisions: Options section only surfaces what exists in the record — never invented
What I Need From You always left blank for user to fill
Brief must be self-contained — external AI needs nothing else
insights: wai-brief + wai-chat-to-track form a complete outbound/inbound pair for external session handoff
